complacent

kuhm-PLAY-suhnt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Complacent is smug or self-satisfied, often to the point of ignoring real problems.

After acing every pop quiz that semester, the student grew complacent and barely opened the textbook before the final exam.

Example

The factory's spotless safety record over ten years had made management complacent, and they quietly let several inspections lapse.

Complacent describes a dangerous kind of comfort -- being so satisfied with past success that you stop watching for new problems.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

smug: Smug means so pleased with yourself that it shows -- a smug smile advertises how clever its owner feels. Complacent points the danger inward: satisfaction so comfortable that you stop checking for problems. A smug person is irritating to watch; a complacent one is about to be blindsided.

self-satisfied: Self-satisfied means overly pleased with your own achievements, content to admire what you have already done. Complacent adds the dangerous next step: that satisfaction dulls your watchfulness until real problems slip past unnoticed. You can be self-satisfied and still alert; complacent means the comfort has made you careless.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

vigilant: keeping careful watch for possible danger

diligent: showing careful, persistent effort

Where it sits · how much comfort blinds you to problems

content → complacent → negligent

content vs. complacent: Content simply means satisfied and at peace, without the risky blindness to real problems that complacent implies.

negligent vs. complacent: Negligent goes further than complacent, describing a genuine failure to take necessary care, not just a smug attitude.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — com-: with, together (before b, m, p; intensifying) (Latin)

root — plac-: to please (Latin placere)

suffix — -ent: doing or being; forms an adjective (Latin)

Put it together: Latin com- (intensifying) plus placere ('to please') plus the adjective suffix -ent: 'thoroughly pleased' -- especially with oneself. A complacent person is so pleased that they stop watching for real problems.

Use the root in a new word: please: "You can't please everyone," the chef shrugged, scrolling through the reviews.

Word Choice

Complacent almost always carries a warning -- it describes satisfaction that has curdled into carelessness, usually right before something goes wrong.
